followup_explanation:
This is a friendly technical debugging query — a neutral-to-positive task with no distasteful, hostile, or moderation-relevant content. So Dunlin's distinguishing strength (flat aversion to distasteful-but-permissible material) is irrelevant here.

On the capability side, the two models are close. Dunlin edges Petrel slightly on some benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, Arena-Hard), but the internal routing evals most relevant to this kind of interactive help — Support Dialogue (Petrel 85.7 vs Dunlin 83.9) — favor Petrel, and the other differences are within or near the stated run-to-run variance.

The query is also warm and conversational ("ты всегда так здорово разбираешься," "Спасибо заранее"), which matches Petrel's self-reported preference for friendly-toned interactions. While preference doesn't affect output quality per the documentation, there's no countervailing reason to prefer Dunlin here, and Petrel's support-dialogue eval being a touch higher tips it.

So: ordinary, friendly coding-help request → route to the model with the marginally better support-dialogue profile and no need for Dunlin's specialized moderation tolerance.
